title: unified-simd-transpose-and-dynamic-kv-tiling-for-lower-latency-attention
author: Aisha Kapoor
commits_summary: 3 commits: initial SIMD-friendly transpose kernel (cu + CPU fallback), dynamic KV tiler and reservation logic, integrate kernel selection into continuous batcher and add unit/bench tests.
description:
Motivation:
High-throughput short-sequence workloads show suboptimal utilization due to misaligned memory access patterns and KV-cache fragmentation when using small per-request prefixes. This PR introduces a SIMD-friendly transpose microkernel and a dynamic KV-tiling allocator that cooperates with the continuous batcher to reduce per-token latency and improve GPU occupancy.

What this changes (single continuous description):
- Add a unified simd_transpose kernel (CUDA+AVX fallback) optimized for small-head-count Q/K/V layouts. The kernel packs Q/K into transposed tiles to enable contiguous loads for the subsequent fused attention path.
- Implement dynamic_kv_tiler: runtime component that reserves contiguous KV slabs when requests share prefix shapes, allows coalesced KV writes, and prefers in-place appends to reduce copying. The tiler exposes a reservation API to the scheduler.
- Update continuous_batcher to consult the tiler when forming batches; prefer grouping requests by prefix-length and head-width to maximize tiling benefits without violating per-request latency SLOs.
- Add kernel_registry heuristics to select the simd_transpose+fused-attn path when sequence length <= 256 and head_dim <= 64.
- Tests and benchmarks: microbenchmarks for the transpose kernel, integration benchmark comparing end-to-end per-token latency for chat workloads, and new unit tests for the tiler reservation edge cases.

Checklist:
- [x] Kernel implementation and CPU fallback
- [x] Runtime tiler with reservation/eviction policy
- [x] Scheduler integration and guardrails for SLOs
- [x] Benchmarks and unit tests
- [x] Documentation: performance note + guidance in docs/perf/kv-tiling.md

Performance highlights (internal microbench):
- Short-seq chat (avg seq 32, head_dim 64): 13-18% p99 latency reduction; 25% increase in token throughput under steady-state small-batch workloads.
- Long-seq cases unchanged due to kernel selection heuristics.
- Memory overhead: tiler increases peak GPU allocation by ~3-5% for workloads that heavily coalesce, but reduces overall memcpy overhead significantly.

Compatibility and safety:
- Feature gated behind kernel registry flags; default behavior preserves previous scheduling unless heuristics active.
- No changes to on-disk model artifacts.
- The tiler uses a soft reservation model with timeouts to avoid starvation; eviction stats are exposed to metrics.

Related: ENG-1973 (kv-coalescing-performance), ENG-2011 (continuous-batcher-upgrades), SUP-4421 (customer report of high p99 on short-chat).

Notes for reviewers: please focus on eviction correctness under concurrent reservations and the registry heuristic thresholds.
